Consult Summary:
- Adult male with 1-week history of painless left elbow swelling and warmth; video exam consistent with probable olecranon bursitis; septic arthritis considered unlikely. Labs ordered to evaluate inflammatory, infectious, rheumatologic, and gout etiologies; start NSAID; return precautions provided and follow-up arranged.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Swelling over the left elbow for ~1 week.
- Symptom characteristics:
  - Painless; feels slightly warm; patient perceives fluid within the swelling.
  - Full range of motion preserved.
  - Mild abnormal sensation/tenderness adjacent to the swelling; tip of elbow non-tender.
  - No known trauma or repetitive physical strain; desk-based job.
  - No prior episodes.
  - Patient reports it “feels a bit better now.”
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Not stated.
- Associated symptoms: No redness reported by patient; no systemic symptoms reported. Dry skin noted over elbow tip on exam.
- Systems review: Not comprehensively documented; denies eczema.
- Timeline: Onset ~1 week ago; currently slightly improved.

Past Medical History:
- Osteoarthritis — patient reports prior GP diagnosis “a few years ago.” No current complications mentioned.

Medications:
- Current: None routinely.
- New recommendation:
  - Ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily (route not documented); take after food; stop if heartburn occurs.
- Allergies:
  - Peanuts (food allergy).
  - No known medication allergies.

Social History:
- Occupation: Desk job.
- Activity: Runs 2–3 times per week; generally fit and well.
- Tobacco/alcohol/substance use: Not documented.

Family History:
- Rheumatologic disease (RA, SLE): Patient unsure; no confirmed family history reported.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Musculoskeletal (video assessment):
  - Left elbow: Visible swelling over olecranon area; warmer than surrounding skin.
  - Minimal tenderness adjacent to swelling; tip of elbow non-tender.
  - Full range of motion preserved.
  - Skin over elbow tip appears dry.
  - Clinician impression: No features suggestive of septic arthritis on current assessment.

Investigations:
- Ordered/planned:
  - Blood tests to assess inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatologic antibodies, and gout (e.g., uric acid).
  - Logistics: Blood test forms to be mailed; results expected ~5–6 days after sampling.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Left olecranon bursitis (probable), non-septic appearance
  - Assessment: 1-week painless swelling with warmth and preserved ROM; no trauma; video exam supportive; septic arthritis unlikely at present.
  - Plan:
    - Start ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily (route not documented); take with food; discontinue if heartburn occurs.
    - Obtain ordered blood tests (inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, gout panel).
    - Follow-up after labs via clinic, video, or phone per patient preference to review results and reassess elbow.
    - Red flags: Seek urgent assessment if elbow becomes very red, very painful, or if redness spreads/worsens.

- Issue 2: Osteoarthritis (history, prior GP diagnosis)
  - Assessment: Stable; no acute management changes discussed.
  - Plan: No specific interventions today; monitor.

General Plan items:
- Forms for blood work to be mailed to patient; patient to arrange sampling promptly.
- Anticipated result turnaround ~5–6 days after specimen collection; patient to contact clinic for follow-up thereafter.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals, comprehensive review of systems, smoking/alcohol/substance use history, full medication reconciliation (patient reports none), immunization status.
- Internal conflicts: Patient age stated as 53, while DOB provided as April 5, 1973 (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor filler/inaudible segments but clinical content adequate.
